top_categories.workout_context: 139ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Bento Gonçalves' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
At GFNY Bento Gonçalves, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at GFNY Bento Gonçalves. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 76 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Bento Gonçalves. Train it until it feels boring.
10,558ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
76 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
10,558ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY Bento Gonçalves. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 10,558ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
